question: Can one identity exactly characterize the left-division image, among finite magmas?
generalProof: Every identity true of all finite reductions of an integer-vector operation holds on the integer operation: use a modulus larger than any nonzero coordinate difference. A real linear functional intertwines division with a*x+b*y for a,b>0. On inputs representing 0 and 1, a term evaluates to zero exactly when its Boolean-OR evaluation is false. Thus every image identity holds on Boolean OR, which lacks left division. This also obstructs any set of identities, although the catalogue records single-equation negatives.
matrixConvention: Source operation is a(T)x+b(T)y. Golden T(x0,x1)=(x1,x0+x1), with T²=T+I. Plastic T(x0,x1,x2)=(x2,x0+x2,x1), with T³=T+I. Both matrices have integral inverses. Reduce coordinates modulo any positive n.
